title: Separate database pool routing for persons and non-persons tables
answers: Which database pool should be used when querying person or distinct ID tables?
Why are there separate persons and non-persons database pools in feature-flags?
Where are queries routed when persons tables are in a separate database?
body:
Database queries must route to the correct pool depending on the table being accessed:
- Persons tables (`posthog_persondistinctid`, `posthog_person`, `posthog_featureflaghashkeyoverride`) must query `DatabasePools.persons_reader` or `DatabasePools.persons_writer`.
- All other tables (teams, feature flags, cohorts) must query `DatabasePools.non_persons_reader` or `DatabasePools.non_persons_writer`.
Enforced in `rust/feature-flags/src/database/postgres_router.rs` and `rust/feature-flags/src/database_pools.rs:DatabasePools`. In split-database deployments, persons data lives on a separate cluster; querying persons tables via non-persons pools causes runtime query failures.
applies: All SQL queries executed by feature-flags services or tests against PostgreSQL.
says: Feature flag evaluation crashes when fetching user identity data in split databases
User cohort lookups fail because queries connect to the wrong database cluster
Route person profile queries to dedicated user database connections during flag checks
Distinct user identity queries fail with missing table errors on separated instances
